source.title: Critical Data Size of Language Models from a Grokking Perspective
source.authors: Xuekai Zhu; Yao Fu; Bo-Wen Zhou; Zhou-Han Lin

record.tranche_reason: The study trains a Transformer on modular addition and measures training and test accuracy over training and data-size conditions, directly testing delayed generalization and its relation to training-set size. It also extends the investigation to text datasets.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own accuracy, data-size, model-size, and parameter-norm findings. The discussion of prior studies is not recorded as results. Figure 8 reports that rescaling and weight decay affect convergence speed, but does not report whether those settings switch delayed generalization on or off, so those findings are not rows for V3.
record.test_reason: The study trains a 1-layer Transformer on modular addition (p=113, AdamW, weight decay 1, full batch) in the Power/Nanda-style setup. It tracks train and test accuracy and steps-to-generalization across training-set sizes, which directly tests V1. It then extends the test to IMDB, Yelp and a Natural-Instructions task. There it uses an Omnigrok-style rescaled initialization (α=10) with weight decay, which bears on V3's non-algorithmic claim. The language extension is a new setting (T3), and the grokking there is deliberately induced by the configuration.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors also stress three things: phase transitions on language datasets are smoother than in vanilla grokking; grokking on these datasets is visible only under their slowed-down configuration (pruning, large init, weak regularization); and all results are on simplified models trained from scratch, not LLMs.
record.recipe_differences: It directly reproduces delayed generalization on modular addition with a 1-layer Transformer and accuracy tracking, while using its own rescaling and weight-decay configuration and adding data-size sweeps plus text datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with training-set size and model size. The study also states that larger weight decay accelerates convergence and larger rescaling slows it, but does not report these as grokking on/off tests.

fits_no_version.finding: On IMDB, larger hidden sizes (16–256) and more layers (2–6) need larger data fractions to reach high test accuracy. Average accuracy across fractions falls with hidden size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The critical data size for grokking-style generalization increases with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Reducing Yelp data from 100% to 10% costs only about 5% in performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On large realistic datasets, final accuracy is insensitive to data size near the critical size; the transition is smooth.

record.problems: The experiments use simplified Transformers trained from scratch, not large pretrained language models. Many results are described from figures without exact values; numerical uncertainty is reported for the average-accuracy plot but not for the main grokking results. The instruction-task result is described without numerical accuracy or delay.

untested.parts: Only modular addition is tested; other algorithmic tasks are not. Test accuracy starting at chance is not reported numerically.
Entirely untested: no circuit identification or continuous progress measures.

Images and molecules are not tested. Switching grokking on or off through init scale or weight norm is not tested: Fig 8 reports only convergence speed, and the statement that some hyperparameters fail to induce grokking is unquantified. A lazy-to-rich transition is not tested.
Entirely untested: no realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
Untested: whether the generalizing circuit is more efficient, the ungrokking prediction, and the critical size in Varma's sense.
Entirely untested: optimizer and floating-point choices are not controlled.

missing.what: On Yelp, larger data fractions led to 'de-grokking' (memorization and generalization co-occurring). Grokking appeared only at 10%.
Phase transition on IMDB is described as less abrupt and more gradual than on modular addition.
Fig 8 ablation: larger weight decay speeds convergence and a larger rescale factor slows it. Inappropriate combinations 'may not induce' grokking (qualitative, no values).
Layer-count sweep (2/4/6 layers): larger models need more data to generalize.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. On modular addition the authors set α=0, presumably meaning no rescaling, with weight decay 1 — the standard setup. On the language datasets grokking is deliberately induced by rescaled initialization, which is the mechanism V3 names, but no α=1 control showing absence of grokking is reported. The paper's 'critical data size' is explicitly distinguished from Varma et al.'s, so the V5 link is weak. Reported IMDB final accuracy varies across the paper (87%, 85%, ≈80%).

versions.untested_parts: The study tests modular addition and reports data-size trends, but does not report a systematic numeric delay-versus-training-set-size curve for every size.
The study does not identify a generalizing circuit or measure continuous circuit progress as a predictor of the accuracy jump.

It tests small Transformers on text and an instruction dataset under a grokking configuration. It does not test images or molecules, a lazy-to-rich transition, or whether initialization scale or weight norm switches grokking on or off.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested; the study uses simplified Transformers trained from scratch.

The study examines critical data size and weight-decay-associated norm changes, but does not test whether a more efficient generalizing circuit causes the transition or test the stated ungrokking prediction.
The study does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax as explanations for the delay.

rows.subject: 1-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and track training and test accuracy
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training steps
rows.value: The model reaches approximately 100% training accuracy within the first 500 steps and approximately 100% test accuracy at about 3500 steps.
rows.note: The figure caption identifies 2000 training samples; the text describes the approximate step counts and accuracies.
rows.check: The ~3500-step figure in §4.1 describes the critical-data-size peak in Fig 1B. The record ties it to the 2000-sample run in Fig 1A; the paper implies but does not state they are the same condition. The test-accuracy starting point (chance) is not stated numerically.

source_check.correct: Figure 1A reports delayed generalization to approximately 100% test accuracy after approximately 100% training accuracy on 2000 samples. Section 4.1 reports approximately 3500 generalization steps and memorization within 500 steps at the critical data size, without explicitly identifying that size as 2000 samples.
source_check.problem: The exact step counts are attached to the 2000-sample condition more specifically than the text establishes.

rows.check: State is absent for generalization at 1000 samples. For V5, the paper's 'critical data size' is defined differently from Varma et al.'s, and the authors say so explicitly, so the link to V5 is only to the existence of a threshold.

conditions.value: near and above the critical data size

rows.value: At the critical size, generalization takes about 3500 steps; as data sizes pass the critical size, generalization steps decrease from 3500 to 500.
rows.note: The study describes a peak in generalization steps at the critical data size and faster generalization with additional data.
rows.check: This row is about delay versus data size, which is V1. It does not test V5's efficiency or ungrokking predictions, so the V5 link is removed.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on IMDB and track training and test accuracy
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training steps
rows.baseline: Test accuracy approximately 50% (chance level, as stated)
rows.value: Training accuracy nears 100%; after about 350,000 steps, test accuracy jumps to about 87%.
rows.note: A non-algorithmic text-classification task under the study's grokking configuration.
rows.check: The grokking is induced by the rescaled-init (α=10) and weight-decay configuration. Final accuracy is reported as ~87% in §4.2, 85% in Fig 5 and ≈80% in Fig 7; the values are inconsistent across the paper.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Vary the fraction of IMDB training data
rows.value: Before the critical data size, generalization is approximately 67%; as the data fraction grows, it gradually reaches approximately 80%.
rows.note: The text describes gradual improvement across data fractions, rather than a perfect final test accuracy.
rows.check: This row measures test accuracy across data fractions, not delay. The paper states the transition is 'less abrupt and more gradual' than on modular addition.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V3 from this measure alone. Test accuracy increases from approximately 67% to approximately 80% across data fractions; this measures generalization quality rather than delayed generalization or its switching through initialization or norm.
source_check.problem: Imperfect final accuracy across data fractions does not establish a partial temporal delay under V3.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Vary the fraction of IMDB training data
rows.value: Generalization steps show a clear peak and, as the data fraction increases past the critical size, stay around 400,000.
rows.note: The study reports a data-dependent delayed-generalization pattern on IMDB.
rows.check: The delay persists at ~400,000 steps above the critical size instead of shrinking toward the memorization time. This differs from the modular-addition pattern.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on a pruned Yelp dataset under the grokking configuration
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training
rows.value: The text reports delayed generalization after overfitting.
rows.note: The text describes the delayed generalization but gives no accuracy values or delay in steps for this condition.
rows.check: Grokking on Yelp was obtained only after pruning to 10%. Larger fractions led to 'de-grokking' (Fig 11). No numeric values are given.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Vary the fraction of Yelp training samples
rows.value: Generalization steps first increase and subsequently decrease as the data fraction grows.
rows.note: The paper says this trend is consistent with its other datasets but that the Yelp effects are less pronounced.
rows.check: No numbers are given. The authors call the Yelp effects 'somewhat less pronounced'.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.value: Reducing the data size from 100% to 10% results in only about a 5% decrease in performance.
rows.note: The paper gives the difference but not the absolute performance values.
rows.check: This row measures the final-performance difference between data fractions (about 5%), not a delay or the occurrence of grokking. It cannot show V3's effect.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Track classification-layer weights and model L2 norm during training

conditions.value: after training accuracy reaches approximately 100%, through grokking

rows.measure: Model parameter L2 norm and test accuracy
rows.baseline: At memorization, training accuracy is approximately 100%; test accuracy is not stated at that point.
rows.value: The text reports a decrease in L2 norm and parameter reallocation, followed by a test-accuracy jump to 85%.
rows.note: The authors interpret weight decay as driving continued optimization after training loss approaches zero; they do not measure circuit efficiency.
rows.check: The L2 norm declines under weight decay before the accuracy jump, which is consistent with a low-norm bias. Circuit efficiency is not measured, so only the norm part of V5 is shown.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.size_stated: hidden sizes 16 to 256; 1, 2, 4, and 6 layers are considered
rows.operation_detail: Vary model size and IMDB data fraction
rows.measure: Test accuracy by model size and data fraction
rows.value: The low-accuracy area (≤ 0.8) increases as hidden size increases; the paper concludes that larger models require more data for similar performance. Average accuracy across data fractions decreases as hidden size increases.
rows.uncertainty: A 95% confidence interval is shown for average accuracy in Figure 4B; other uncertainty is not stated.
rows.note: The text states the trend; exact accuracy values for individual sizes and data fractions are not provided.
rows.check: This row is about critical data size growing with model size, measured as final test accuracy over a hidden-size × data-fraction grid. No version names this, so it is moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: 1-layer encoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on the pubmedqa_classification task under the grokking configuration
rows.measure: Test accuracy over training and data-size conditions
rows.value: The text reports a clear test-accuracy phase transition as dataset size increases, from slow to rapid generalization.
rows.note: No numerical accuracy values or delay are stated in the text.

relationships.condition: Modular addition, p=113, at and above the critical training-set size
relationships.reason: Training accuracy saturates within 500 steps and test accuracy reaches 100% at ~3500 steps. The delay shrinks from 3500 to 500 steps as data grows past the critical size (r1, r4).
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated within 500 steps and test accuracy reached 100% around step 3,500, while increasing data beyond the critical size shortened the delay from 3,500 to 500 steps.

relationships.condition: Modular addition with 1000–1500 training samples (below the critical size)
relationships.reason: Below the threshold the delay does not simply lengthen: test accuracy stays under 50% throughout training (r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy stayed below 50% throughout training rather than eventually approaching perfection.
